item.title: The 1973 Oil Crisis Still Matters Today
item.description: Author Philip Delves Broughton is on Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss his new book, Embargo, and how the 1973 oil crisis transformed Saudi Arabia’s economic and political power while exposing the world’s vulnerability to turmoil in the Middle East. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Delves Broughton examines parallels with today’s Iran conflict, US involvement in Venezuela and Saudi Arabia’s continuing effort to diversify its economy beyond oil. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Crisis Reshapes Washington’s Tech Debate
item.description: Veda Partners’ Henrietta Treyz and Washington Post national security reporter Tara Copp are on Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss how the Nvidia crisis is fueling bipartisan scrutiny of chip export controls and raising national security concerns about the Pentagon’s reliance on advanced technology. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Treyz and Copp also examine the prospects for congressional investigations and tighter chip restrictions, as well as funding battles over the FAA and the continuing US conflict with Iran. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Router Failure Exposes Risks in FAA Network
item.description: Former TSA Administrator and FBI Deputy Director John Pistole is on Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss the nationwide FAA ground stop and the vulnerabilities exposed by a router failure during work on the agency’s aging telecommunications network. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Pistole examines the need for greater redundancy, questions surrounding contractor L3Harris and concerns about whether the system can withstand another disruption as Thanksgiving travel approaches. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic IPO Arrives at a Pivotal AI Moment
item.description: Bloomberg News senior equities reporter Bailey Lipschultz and Bloomberg Intelligence’s Mandeep Singh are on Bloomberg This Weekend to examine Anthropic’s potentially record-setting IPO and how Nvidia’s upheaval following Jensen Huang’s departure is changing the outlook for AI investment and computing capacity. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, they discuss Anthropic’s roughly $1.4 trillion targeted valuation, investor demand and compute costs, as well as what its market debut could signal for OpenAI and the broader AI trade. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Crisis Complicates Trump’s China Trip
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, co-host of Bloomberg Surveillance Annmarie Hordern examines how scrutiny surrounding Nvidia and Jensen Huang is shifting the focus of President Donald Trump’s China trip from trade toward chip export controls and questions about how restricted technology may have reached China. Speaking with host Christina Ruffini, Hordern also discusses mounting pressure on the Commerce Department and how the controversy could lead Congress to pursue tighter controls on advanced chips and computing power. (Source: Bloomberg)
